00 · Start here
A growth breakdown for Flick
Why we made this

Your launch post did 618K views on X, and your bio ends on the whole idea: create on Flick, watch on Flick TV. With festival entries closing on 15 December, this board is how we would bring the people who already binge AI series on TikTok to both sides of that line.

It is free. Take whatever is useful.

How to read this board
Use the list on the left, or press P to go frame by frame. On a phone, just scroll.
Creator cards: platform, followers and median views on recent videos.
Please note
Made by hypjam from public information, checked 23 Oct 2026. Nobody at Flick asked for this, and it is not paid work. The creators named here have not been contacted and have no link to hypjam: they show the kind of people we would cast.
12 AI storytellers shortlisted, 4 scripts with 32 hooks, and a plan to fill Flick TV before your festival deadline.
Four numbers to remember
618K: views on your launch post on X, 14 May
53 days: from today to your 15 December festival deadline
20+: festival awards won by the first 4 films made with Flick
32: hooks written across 4 scripts
Who made this

hypjam is a UGC agency in London. We cast, script, direct and edit creators for consumer startups, and run the best videos as ads.

01 · Why UGC
Why creator videos work
Authenticity
People trust people
A studio saying "direct films, not clips" is a claim. A filmmaker showing the canvas, the shot list and the cut behind their latest short is proof.
Show, do not tell
The film is the demo
AI film sells itself in the first second. The finished scene first, then ten seconds of how it was directed, does what a feature list cannot.
Objections
Answer "is it slop?" out loud
It is a common first comment under AI films. A creator showing the script, the blocking and the takes they threw away answers it on camera.
A real deadline
Festival entries close 15 December
A date creators can count down to. Making-of posts from entrants give people a reason to start a film on Flick this month, not next year.
Fuel for ads
Your best ads come from creators
The strongest creator videos become partnership ads. We test 8 openings per script, so the budget follows what people actually watch.
Doesn't feel like an ad
Part 1 is a normal post
AI series creators already post Part 1 and promise Part 2. Sending viewers to Flick TV for the rest is the same post, labelled as an ad.
02 · What we learned
Where Flick is today
The studio
Script, generate and edit on one canvas, from idea to final cut: the Flick agent to ideate, camera control and consistent characters, 3D Stage to block scenes, an AI video editor, and 1.5M+ visual references on Flickpedia. Free to start.
The watch side
Flick TV shows films made with Flick. Viewers watch, like, comment and tip in credits, and Get Workflow opens the canvas behind a film, prompts included. Creators can cash out eligible tips, and publishing shares to TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and X from the same screen.
Your own channels
@flickartHQ on X: 37 posts in the last 14 days, from festival news to new models and film breakdowns. Discord: about 4,260 members. Plus a Filmmaker Residency, a Creative Partner Program and tutorials on YouTube.
Already working
  • Your launch post: 618K views on X (14 May). $6M raised, 14 filmmakers, 13 films, all made on Flick.
  • The first 4 films made with Flick won 20+ awards at international festivals.
  • Backed by True Ventures, GV, Lightspeed and YC.
What that tells us
The work travels: your launch post reached about 194 times your follower count. What is missing is volume: storytellers outside your community posting Flick films every week, and sending their viewers to Flick TV.
The timing
Festival entries close on 15 December. Every entry must be posted publicly with the festival watermark and tagged to your accounts, and every entry is published to Flick TV, where Audience Choice is voted on from 6 to 19 January.
Sources: flick.art (home, Flick TV, festival and rules, Residency, Creative Partners, About, Docs), the YC company and launch pages, YC job posts, Flick's X profile and posts, and Discord's public invite count, all read 23 Oct 2026.

04 · The objection
"Is it real filmmaking?": the objection to win
A common first comment under AI films is "slop". Your whole pitch answers it: you handle the AI, they direct the film. So the videos should show the directing.
What you already say
  • "We Handle AI. You Direct Films."
  • "AI doesn't replace your creativity; it listens, it follows."
  • Your festival judges story first, and "thoughtful use of AI" over which tools were used.
What a creator can show
  • The script: one page, turned into shots on the canvas.
  • The blocking: a camera set in 3D Stage before anything is generated.
  • The same face: one character reference held across every shot.
  • The receipts: Get Workflow, prompts included.
The answer that is yours
A film on Flick TV can carry its own workflow. Nobody has to take a creator's word for how it was made: viewers can open the canvas and see every choice.
How we use it
Script A ends on the workflow. Script B is a writer directing their own pages. Every script shows at least one choice the creator made, never just the result.
The second question: is it allowed?
Your festival rules already rule out other people's characters, brands and music, and real people's faces or voices without consent. Every paid video here follows the same rules.
What creators never say
No "replace Hollywood" and no "no skills needed". No earnings or prize promises beyond your own pages. The AI label on, always.
05 · Audience
Who to sell to first
Start here
Storytellers with a script and no budget
Writers, film students and indie filmmakers. Flick takes them from idea to script, storyboard, shots and the edit in one workspace. Formats A and B.
Start here
AI series makers
They already post in parts and episodes to big audiences. Flick gives them one canvas for every episode, and Flick TV for the whole run. Formats A and C.
Close behind
Festival entrants
Anyone making a film before 15 December, from first-timers to working directors. Free to enter, with categories from vertical drama to animation. Format D.
Second
People who binge AI series
The viewers who comment "Part 2?". They come to Flick TV for the rest of the story, and some of them start making their own. Format C.
Where we would start
Makers first, watchers close behind. Your YC page and your launch both lead with filmmakers, and every film on Flick TV starts with someone making it on Flick. So month one sells the studio to storytellers and series makers, and Format C starts sending their viewers to Flick TV.
06 · The moment
Seven weeks to the festival deadline
Festival entries close on 15 December, and every entry is posted publicly and lands on Flick TV. Creator videos started now ride that wave instead of waiting for it.
Now to 1 November
Halloween shorts. Creators post horror shorts made in Flick, with the full film on Flick TV, where Horror and thriller already has its own tab. The first partnership ad tests go live.
November
Festival diaries. Creators post their entry week by week: the idea, the script, the blocking, the cut. Budget moves to the winning hooks.
15 December to 20 January
Entries close, and Audience Choice voting runs on Flick TV from 6 to 19 January. Creators ask their followers to watch and vote, right up to the premiere on 20 January.
What this needs from you
  • A Flick account with credits for each signed creator
  • A tracking link per creator, to sign-up or a film's Flick TV page
  • Your call on whether campaign films may enter the festival
Why start now
Halloween is eight days away and the festival deadline is seven weeks out. Started now, the hooks are tested by the time entrants are choosing a tool.
07 · The first month
Your first four weeks
Week 1 · 26 Oct-1 Nov
You approve the shortlist and the 4 formats. We sign creators, set up their Flick accounts and send each one a script with 8 hooks. Halloween shorts go first.
Week 2 · 2-8 Nov
First videos in, each reviewed within 48 hours. Series creators publish full episodes on Flick TV, and the best cuts start as partnership ad tests on TikTok and Meta.
Week 3 · 9-15 Nov
We double down on the hooks and creators that drive sign-ups and move budget off the rest. Festival diary posts begin.
Week 4 · 16-22 Nov
Results review together: sign-ups, paid plans and Flick TV views by creator and by ad, and the plan for the run to 15 December.
If it is a yes this week
Agreement signed and creators set up by Friday. First videos live within 14 days of the scripts being signed off.

Takeaway
The biggest numbers here are Part 1s and Episode 1s, often from small accounts. So we would run many series creators side by side, testing 8 hooks per script, and send their viewers to Flick TV for the rest.
Where the market is
The audience for AI series already exists on TikTok, spread across many accounts and many parts. Flick TV gives it one place to land: the whole series, a tip for the maker, and the workflow behind it.
10 · Script A
Script A: Take my workflow
The brief

Where: TikTok and Instagram Reels on the creator's own account, then the best cut as a partnership ad (TikTok Spark Ads and Meta) pointing to flick.art

Length: 30-40s master. 15s ad cut: shots 1, 2, 3 and 7.

Goal: Sign-ups at flick.art, and workflows taken on Flick TV

Who films it: An AI filmmaker who already posts mini-movies or series (for example @aidsgns, @until.her or @dreamfall.art), making a new short with original characters entirely in Flick and publishing it to Flick TV with workflow sharing on. Screen recordings of their own Flick canvas and Flick TV page, plus the finished film.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. You can open the exact canvas this film came fromYou can open the exact canvas this film came from. Here it is.

  4. The part of an AI film nobody shows youThis is the part of an AI film nobody shows you.
  5. [N] shots. One canvas.[N] shots, one canvas, and I'll show you all of it.
  6. Stop asking for my promptsStop asking for my prompts. Here's the whole canvas.
  7. You watched it. Now take it apart.You watched it. Now take it apart.
  8. Comment WORKFLOW and I'll send the linkWant the whole canvas? Comment workflow.

11 · Script B
Script B: Script to screen
The brief

Where: TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts on the creator's own account, then the best cut as a partnership ad on TikTok and Meta pointing to flick.art

Length: 35-45s master. 15s ad cut: shots 1, 5 and 7.

Goal: Sign-ups at flick.art from writers and filmmakers

Who films it: A writer or filmmaker with a script of their own (for example @paul.screenwriter or @until.her), or an AI how-to creator such as @dawoodzahidd working from a short scene. They direct one page in Flick, with original characters, and film the page itself next to the laptop.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. I wrote this scene. Then I directed it with AI.I wrote this scene, and then I directed it with AI.
  2. One page of script. [Time].One page of my script, [time], and this is what came out.
  3. A screenwriter directs their own pagesI write scripts. I've never directed one of my own pages. Until now.
  4. I blocked this shot before I generated itI blocked this shot in 3D before I generated a single frame.
  5. Same character. Every shot.The hardest part of AI film is keeping a face the same. Watch.
  6. It started as INT. KITCHEN, NIGHTThis started as three words on a page. Interior, kitchen, night.
  7. This isn't prompting. It's directing.This isn't prompting. This is directing.
  8. Would you watch the rest of this film?Would you watch the rest of this film? Be honest.

16 · Ads
How the paid ads would run
1 · Film
Each script is shot once, with 8 different openings.
→
2 · Launch
Each opening runs as its own ad, from the creator's handle as a partnership ad.
→
3 · Read
After a few days we compare cost per sign-up and how many people watch past 3 seconds.
4 · Cut
The weakest openings switch off and the budget moves to the best two.
→
5 · Remix
Winning hooks get new bodies and new creators.
→
6 · Refresh
New creator videos every week, so the ads never go stale.
Where the ads point
flick.art, with one tracking link per creator that lands on sign-up or on the film's Flick TV page, so every sign-up traces back to the video that drove it.
Why partnership ads
Ads that run from a creator's own handle look like that creator's post, not a brand ad. That is the format these videos are built for.
What we would need
Access to your TikTok and Meta ad accounts (or we run them from ours), your pixel on sign-up and first purchase, and a weekly look at sign-ups and Flick TV views.
17 · Process
How a campaign runs, step by step
1 · Brief
You tell us the goal, the audience and what can and can't be said about Flick.
→
2 · Cast
We shortlist creators by niche, location and median views. You pick.
→
3 · Offer
We send each creator the brief, the dates and the rate.
4 · Sign
A written agreement with every creator, covering usage and disclosure.
→
5 · Scripts
One per format: 8 hooks, a shot list, screens to record and a caption.
→
6 · Film and upload
Creators film on their phones and upload to a private folder only we see.
7 · Review
We check every video within 48 hours. Nothing posts unapproved.
→
8 · Post
On the creator's own account, with the ad disclosure and the paid-partnership label.
→
9 · Pay and report
Creators paid within 7 days of going live. You get a report every Monday.
Where creators talk to us
One hypjam Discord for every creator. Each campaign gets a private channel group for chat, scripts and posted links that only its creators and your team can see.
Creator access
Each signed creator makes their film inside Flick on an account you set up, and publishes it to Flick TV with workflow sharing on, so everything on screen is the real product. We track usage and hand the accounts back after the campaign.
18 · Reporting
What we report, and when
Every video
Views, how many people stay past 3 seconds, average watch time, saves, shares and comments.
Every creator link
A tracking link for each creator, so sign-ups trace back to the video that drove them.
Every Monday
A short report: every video, the hooks that won, sign-ups by creator, and what we change next.
Every month
A review call: spend, sign-ups, cost per result on anything run as an ad, and the plan for next month.
19 · Rules
Rules we never break
Disclosure
"Ad | Paid partnership with Flick" on screen, said in the first seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. That is what the FTC asks for.
Who films
Adults only (18+). Creators use Flick themselves before they talk about it.
What gets said
Nothing your own pages do not say Flick does. No invented numbers. We never pay for a positive opinion, only for the video.
AI label
Every AI-made video carries the platform's AI-generated label and says "Made with Flick" in the caption.
Original work only
Original characters and worlds only: no real person's face or voice without their written OK, and no characters, brands, music or footage someone else owns. Your festival rules ask the same.
How we run it
Every video reviewed within 48 hours before it posts. Creators paid within 7 days of going live.

21 · Questions
Questions for you
Q1
Which side do you want to grow first in month one: people making films on Flick, or people watching on Flick TV?
Q2
What counts as a win: sign-ups, paid plans, films published to Flick TV, or festival entries?
Q3
Can each signed creator get a Flick account with credits for the campaign?
Q4
Should films made for this campaign be entered in the festival, or kept separate from it?
Q5
Should this run next to your Creative Partner Program, with the best creators moving into it afterwards?
Q6
Which features should every video show, and is the agent that edits a video by itself shipping before 15 December?
Q7
Organic only, or do you want to run the best videos as partnership ads?
Q8
Who signs off scripts, and who else decides on the budget?
